summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma, chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and diastolic heart failure, was admitted for hypotension and fatigue discovered during a clinic visit. Initial evaluation revealed acute kidney injury likely due to hypovolemia, possibly from medication non-compliance or inadvertent diuresis. He received a fluid bolus and a unit of packed red blood cells for anemia. Blood and urine cultures showed no infection. His blood pressure and renal function improved with supportive care. Cardiology recommended reducing carvedilol from 25mg BID to 12.5mg BID and switching furosemide from BID to daily dosing while discontinuing spironolactone. He was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and close follow-up planned.
